safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce from SAP 3.0 days to recommended 1.83 days

narrative: Material PL1__M35F13F0 shows moderate demand variability (CV=0.33) with all 137 working days having positive demand, indicating a stable, continuously consumed item requiring ~100,061 units annually. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.65) due to a bimodal pattern alternating between ~1-day express and ~3-day standard deliveries, which drives a high sigma_LTD of 887 units and necessitates a safety stock of 1,459 units for 95% service level. The unconstrained EOQ of 20,817 units is hard-capped by the 5,981-unit storage limit to 4,522 units, yielding 22 replenishment orders per year. The recommended (r,Q) policy delivers a 58% total cost reduction versus the current SAP baseline while fully respecting storage constraints.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review with EOQ-derived fixed order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (100% non-zero working days) with moderate variability, making a continuous-review fixed-Q policy optimal. EOQ balances ordering and holding costs under the hard storage capacity ceiling, and the MOQ of 1,771 is comfortably below the capacity-constrained Q of 4,522.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 5,981 units binds hard against the unconstrained EOQ of 20,817 units, forcing a 78% reduction in order quantity. This raises annual order frequency from ~5 to ~22 orders/year. Relaxing storage by ~15,000 units would recover approximately 70% of the theoretical cost optimum.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None — MOQ (1,771) + safety stock (1,459) = 3,230 units, which is below max_storage_units (5,981). Policy is fully feasible with no MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
